title: Array Data Structure
summary: An array is a fundamental linear data structure that stores elements of the same type in contiguous memory locations under a single variable name.

What is an Array?.definition: A collection of items stored at contiguous memory locations, identifiable by indices.
key_points: Elements are placed side by side in memory without gaps.
Provides predictable memory layout and cache friendliness.
Analogy: A numbered row of storage lockers or passenger train compartments.
Programming example: let scores = [85, 92, 78, 95];
What is an Array?.visual_cues: Row of connected boxes, locker doors with labels, memory block visualization.

Index-Based Access.definition: Accessing any array element directly using its numerical position, starting from index 0.
key_points: Zero-based indexing: the first item is at index 0 because offset from the start is zero.
Direct access formula: memory address = base_address + (index * element_size).
Instant time complexity: O(1) constant time access.
Programming example: let first = scores[0];
Index-Based Access.visual_cues: Index tags below each cell, pointer jumping directly to index without inspecting earlier cells.

Insertion.definition: Adding a new element into the array at the start, end, or a specific middle index.
key_points: Inserting at the end is instant if space permits.
Inserting in the middle requires shifting existing items to the right to open a spot.
Worst-case time complexity: O(n) when inserting at the beginning due to shifting all items.
Resulting array increases in logical length by one.
Insertion.visual_cues: New element descending, elements sliding right sequentially, element settling into vacant cell.

Deletion.definition: Removing an element from a specific index in the array.
key_points: Removing an element leaves a vacant space that must be filled.
Subsequent elements shift left by one position to maintain contiguous storage.
Time complexity: O(n) for front/middle deletion, O(1) for removing the last item.
Resulting array decreases in logical length by one.
Deletion.visual_cues: Target cell fading out, remaining elements sliding left to close gap, cleaned-up array.

Traversal.definition: Visiting every element of an array sequentially from start to finish.
key_points: Iterates from index 0 to length - 1 using a loop.
Used for reading values, calculating sums, or updating elements.
Time complexity: O(n) because each of the n elements is visited once.
Programming example: for(let i = 0; i < scores.length; i++) { print(scores[i]); }
Traversal.visual_cues: Active scanning highlight traveling smoothly from left to right, inspecting each value.

Search.definition: Finding the location of a target value within the array.
key_points: Linear search inspects elements one by one starting from index 0.
If target matches, the search halts and returns the matching index.
If the end of array is reached without a match, returns not found (-1).
Time complexity: O(n) in worst case (element at end or absent).
Search.visual_cues: Magnifying glass/target probe comparing each box to target; green checkmark on match or red indicator on finish.
